test_title: SSC MTS Previous Year Paper (Held on: 18 Oct 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A sum of ₹ 15,400 was lent in two parts, partly at 9% and the rest at 12% simple interest. The total interest received after three years is ₹ 4,914. The ratio of the money lent at 9% to that at 12% is:
solution:
**Given:**

Sum = Rs. 15400

Interest rates are 9% and 12%

Total interest = Rs. 4914

Time = 3 year

**Concept used:**

S.I = (P × R × T)/100

**Calculation:**

Let the sum lent at 9% is Rs. x then lent at 12% is Rs. (15400 - x)

S.I at 9% = (x × 9 × 3)/100

⇒ Rs. 27x/100

Now, S.I at 12% = [(15400 - x) × 12 × 3]/100

⇒ Rs. 36(15400 - x)/100 

According to question ,

(27x/100) + 36(15400 - x)/100 = 4914 

⇒ (27x - 36x + 554400)/100 = 4914

⇒ - 9x + 554400 = 491400 

⇒ 9x = 63000 

⇒ x = 7000

So, sum lent at 9% is Rs. 7000 and sum lent at 12% is = Rs. 8400

The ratio between them = 7000 : 8400

⇒ 5 : 6

**∴ Required ratio is 5 : 6**
